record.paper_title: Some open problems of graph theory.
record.original_question: Given a finite set of integers, decide whether there exists a bipartite graph whose list of vertex degrees is exactly that set of integers.

evidence.quote: Problem 7. (R. I. Tyshkevich) On recognizing whether for a set of integers there exists a bipartite graph for which that set is the list of vertex-degrees.

artifact.self_contained_problem: For a graph $G$, let the degree set $D(G)$ denote the set of distinct vertex degrees occurring in $G$. Given a finite nonempty set $S$ of positive integers, design an algorithm (or give a characterization) that decides whether there exists a simple bipartite graph $G$ such that $D(G) = S$, i.e., the set of vertex degrees of $G$ equals exactly $S$.
artifact.status_search_result: The recognition question for bipartite degree sets is settled: it is known that for every finite nonempty set S of positive integers there exists a bipartite graph G with D(G) = S. This is established in the literature on bipartite graphs and their degree sets (e.g., Manoussakis and Patil, "Bipartite graphs and their degree sets," and subsequent works on minimum orders of such bipartite graphs). Hence the recognition problem has a trivial affirmative answer, and refinements (minimum order, connectedness, unicyclic, etc.) have also been characterized.

status_evidence.title: Bipartite Graphs and their Degree Sets
status_evidence.snippet: Given a finite, nonempty set S of positive integers, it is shown that there exists a bipartite graph G such that D(G) = S.
status_evidence.claim: Every finite nonempty set of positive integers is the degree set of some bipartite graph, settling the recognition problem affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: On degree sets and the minimum orders in bipartite graphs
status_evidence.snippet: For a given pair (S,T) of finite nonempty sets of positive integers, there exists a bipartite graph B(X,Y) with D(X)=S, D(Y)=T; minimum orders are determined.
status_evidence.claim: Refined results determine minimum orders for bipartite graphs realizing prescribed degree sets, building on the affirmative resolution.
